defects.description: PRESENT: replacement plates do not completely eliminate source-background objects. Detached-looking hardware and dark clothing-like masses remain beside the performer.
defects.evidence: S03@00:11.750: knob-like object outside screen-right wrist. S06@00:16.250: dark hanging mass at lower right. S12@00:41.750: dark protrusion beside right hip.
defects.recommended_action: Remove residual source objects with object-aware holdouts and review the complete moving silhouette at native frame rate.

defects.description: PRESENT: Look 2 reads as washed gray, heavily outlined denim rather than restrained French black denim. S01 is especially far from the product reference.
defects.evidence: S01@00:01.250: bright marbled jacket and gray jeans. S03@00:07.250: darker but strongly etched jacket. S04@00:12.750: prominent bright buttons and contrast seams.
defects.recommended_action: Regenerate against the black-denim product material, seam contrast and hardware finish; approve one outfit before propagation.

defects.description: PRESENT: the pre-hook center panel still reads as an architectural recess, not a mirror multiplying the key highlight. Hook mirror multiplication is visible.
defects.evidence: S01@00:01.750 and S04@00:12.750 show a dark divided rectangle without a repeated highlight; S06@00:17.250 shows multiple panels repeating bright diagonals.
defects.recommended_action: Make the single pre-hook panel optically reflective while retaining the approved room and subsequent multi-panel progression.

defects.description: PRESENT: reference-level hardware and pocket detailing remain inaccurate. S01 also adds a red pocket tab absent from the supplied product.
defects.evidence: S01@00:02.750: red tab and highly distressed-looking pocket edging. S04@00:13.250: blank bright discs replace the reference's restrained metal-button detail.
defects.recommended_action: Remove the unreferenced tab and restore exact pocket flaps, button proportions and subdued hardware detailing.

defects.description: PRESENT: pre-hook edges retain gray fringes and soft contamination. Their changing thickness around moving clothing reads as extraction rather than motivated rim light.
defects.evidence: S01@00:02.750: fuzzy screen-right shoulder. S03@00:10.750: uneven sleeve and shoulder boundary. S04@00:13.750: pale echoes beside lowered sleeve.
defects.recommended_action: Rebuild motion-aware alpha edges and decontaminate foreground color without uniformly feathering the silhouette.

defects.description: PRESENT: the pre-hook jacket resets across assets. Wash, pocket shape, hardware brightness and sleeve fit change; S04 does not look like merely a crop of S03's outfit.
defects.evidence: S01@00:03.250 has pale textured denim and a red tab; S03@00:06.250 has darker, looser construction; S04@00:12.250 introduces cleaner flaps and brighter buttons.
defects.recommended_action: Propagate a single approved Look 2 construction through all three performance ranges; derive S04's crop after wardrobe continuity is locked.

defects.description: PRESENT: the insert enlarges a soft generated jacket torso instead of delivering product-true hardware macro photography. Blank buttons and outlined seams weaken the commercial purpose.
defects.evidence: S02@00:04.250 and S02@00:05.750 show a broad chest crop with featureless button discs; the slow enlargement does not reveal credible hardware detail.
defects.recommended_action: Replace with a reference-grounded hardware macro retaining the specified cold lighting and slow push.

defects.description: PRESENT: source-background contamination persists beside pre-hook sleeves, including a discrete knob-like remnant. It is not part of the replacement room.
defects.evidence: S03@00:06.250: white sliver between torso and screen-right sleeve. S03@00:09.750: dark rounded projection outside the cuff. S03@00:11.750: projection remains exposed beside the wrist.
defects.recommended_action: Rotoscope the arm-to-torso gaps and remove attached background components independently of garment alpha.

defects.description: PRESENT: body coverage is largely intact, but broad pale silhouette echoes remain during hook movement. Matte v3 has not produced believable moving boundaries.
defects.evidence: S06@00:17.750: extra pale shape outside screen-left upper arm. S08@00:24.250: rectangular pale extension beyond crossed forearm. S08@00:26.750: shoulder-adjacent pale projection.
defects.recommended_action: Separate genuine motion blur from retained foreground/background echoes; rebuild alpha around each affected gesture.

defects.description: PRESENT: early-hook construction remains non-reference. S06 is cropped and deeply unzipped with exposed shirt hem; S08 has contrasting pale sleeves and a different closure. Required inside-sleeve navy stripes are not established.
defects.evidence: S06@00:17.250 exposes tie nearly to the waist and shirt below the hem; S08@00:24.750 shows pale sleeves, dark zipper and dark pocket outlines.
defects.recommended_action: Restore reference jacket length, closed front, restrained shirt exposure, mastic sleeves and correctly placed inner-sleeve stripes.

defects.description: PRESENT: early-hook branding is gold and wearer-left, but letterforms remain malformed and unstable. Correct location does not make the mark product-true.
defects.evidence: S06@00:19.250: compressed irregular glyphs. S08@00:24.750 and S08@00:25.250: visibly different letter grouping and spacing on the same chest stripe.
defects.recommended_action: Replace generated text with approved artwork, tracked to the cloth with perspective, folds and occlusion.

defects.description: PRESENT, changed manifestation: the old navy shoulder blocking is gone, but the hook still substitutes incompatible jacket variants. Ribbed cuffs, oversized collars and differing stripe depths remain.
defects.evidence: S09@00:30.250: pronounced ribbed cuffs and close-fitting waist. S11@00:35.750: tall flared collar, deeper chest band and sweatshirt-like fabric.
defects.recommended_action: Use the same product-approved cotton jacket construction across every hook shot, not independent interpretations.

defects.description: PRESENT: branding still resets between hook shots. S11's former centered white lettering is gone, but it now introduces stacked gold pseudo-text rather than the consistent single-line wordmark.
defects.evidence: S09@00:31.250: tiny single-line mark. S11@00:33.750: stacked gold marks. S12@00:39.750: larger horizontal glyph string returns.
defects.recommended_action: Apply one approved wordmark asset and garment-relative scale across all hook assets.

defects.description: PRESENT: the two-look color strategy reads, but Look 1 is still several approximate beige/navy garments. The requested closed track jacket and reference collar, sleeves, pockets and hem are not consistently realized.
defects.evidence: S06@00:20.250: shortened open-front jacket. S08@00:25.750: two-tone sleeve/body treatment. S12@00:40.750: large pale flared collar and exposed shirt cuffs.
defects.recommended_action: Approve a full-outfit hero frame against both references, then preserve its construction throughout the hook.

defects.description: PRESENT: the delicate reference typography is unfulfilled throughout the hook, including S12. Some marks become illegible pseudo-text; S11 changes the wordmark's layout entirely.
defects.evidence: S09@00:30.750: compressed unreadable mark. S11@00:36.250: multiple short gold rows. S12@00:40.250: malformed horizontal lettering.
defects.recommended_action: Replace all generative lettering with the reference's single-line typographic treatment and validate at delivery resolution.

defects.description: PRESENT: the jacket changes across the city cutaway. The specific old pointed-collar reset is repaired, but length, sleeves, zipper, pockets and shirt exposure still reset.
defects.evidence: S06@00:21.250: cropped jacket, exposed shirt hem and cuffs. S08@00:23.750: longer body, pale sleeves, dark zipper and outlined pockets.
defects.recommended_action: Carry S06's corrected product construction into S08 using shared garment topology and appearance constraints.

defects.description: PRESENT: hook-return contamination remains outside the body. The exact source object is UNCERTAIN, low confidence, but these attached shapes do not belong to the mirror plate.
defects.evidence: S08@00:23.750: black-and-white fragment behind screen-right flank. S08@00:24.250: pale rectangular material protrudes beyond the moving forearm.
defects.recommended_action: Re-extract the hook-return foreground with explicit exclusion masks for attached source material.

defects.description: PRESENT: non-room material is still visible at the immediate hook return, behind the screen-right waist. Its precise source identity remains uncertain.
defects.evidence: S08@00:23.750 shows a bright-edged dark fragment in the gap between the screen-right jacket flank and arm, interrupting the reflected floor.
defects.recommended_action: Patch the return-frame waist/arm gap and propagate the exclusion through the following gesture.

defects.description: PRESENT: late-hook outfit resets remain conspicuous. S08/S09 changes sleeve color and cuff construction; S11/S12 changes tie pattern, collar edging and cuff exposure without a specified wardrobe change.
defects.evidence: S08@00:29.250: pale straight sleeves. S09@00:29.750: mastic sleeves with ribbed cuffs. S12@00:39.750: thin-striped dark tie and exposed white cuffs replace S11's styling.
defects.recommended_action: Lock the complete outfit, including shirt and tie, across all hook shots before compositing.

defects.description: PRESENT, partially improved: navy shoulder coverage and S12's shirt-style jacket front are gone. Late-hook collars, ribbed construction and missing inner-sleeve stripe detail still do not match the product.
defects.evidence: S09@00:30.250 shows ribbed cuffs; S11@00:34.250 shows an exaggerated flared collar; S12@00:41.250 shows pale collar lining and plain visible sleeves.
defects.recommended_action: Correct collar height/lining, cotton cuff and hem construction, and sleeve stripe placement from the supplied detail references.

defects.description: PRESENT: late performance retains large trailing patches and jagged extrusions outside intact anatomy. These are more severe than a subtle edge halo.
defects.evidence: S11@00:34.750: stair-stepped protrusions along screen-right shoulder and sleeve. S11@00:36.750: broad pale patch behind screen-left shoulder. S12@00:40.750: pale shoulder echo.
defects.recommended_action: Remove trailing source regions with temporally tracked masks; preserve only genuine garment silhouette and motion blur.

defects.description: PRESENT, reduced manifestation: a label/content discrepancy remains at the diamond cut. The earlier approximately one-frame offset is not established by this strip.
defects.evidence: The frame labeled S04@00:14.750 already contains S05's diamond, while the declared S05 boundary is 00:14.754. This is a 0.004-second nominal discrepancy, not proof of audible mistiming.
defects.recommended_action: Generate shot labels from actual encoded frame ownership and reconcile nominal seconds with frame presentation timestamps.

defects.description: PRESENT: narrow soft gray fringes remain even where late-hook masks do not have larger protrusions. Cap and sleeve boundaries still contrast poorly with the sharp background plate.
defects.evidence: S09@00:29.750: pale cap crown outline. S11@00:35.250: soft sleeve boundary. S12@00:41.250: luminous fringe along screen-right arm.
defects.recommended_action: Refine edge color and alpha locally after repairing broad leaks; do not substitute blanket blur.

defects.description: OPEN: one-native-frame synchronization, beat landings and the final hard out remain UNCERTAIN, low confidence. Silent two-fps samples cannot certify these gates.
defects.evidence: S06@00:15.750 captures white flash; S12@00:42.750 is the final supplied performance sample. Neither exposes audio alignment or the encoded 00:43.279 endpoint.
defects.recommended_action: Audit the native-frame export with audio against the song clock, including all cuts and the final hit.

defects.description: OPEN: returns to performance are visible, but exact lip and gesture synchronization after inserts remains UNCERTAIN, low confidence. No audible sync failure is demonstrated.
defects.evidence: S03@00:06.250, S08@00:23.750 and S11@00:33.750 show performance returning after cutaways; half-second spacing cannot resolve a one-frame timing gate.
defects.recommended_action: Compare each performance return with the untouched source at the requested source/song mapping.

defects.description: OPEN: crossed-arm intent is present, but the unusual one-second asset trim is not source-clock verified. Confidence in exact in-point conformance is low.
defects.evidence: S09@00:29.750 and S09@00:30.750 show crossed arms and a downward head movement, compatible with the source contact sheet but insufficient to prove master 75.868 seconds.
defects.recommended_action: Verify decoded source-frame correspondence at the S09 in-point and out-point.

defects.description: PARTIALLY RESOLVED: the corridor is now clearly visible; the previous all-white sampled state is gone. Strobe cadence and the requested glitch transition remain UNCERTAIN, low confidence at two fps.
defects.evidence: S10@00:31.750 and S10@00:32.750 show the reflective corridor; S10@00:33.250 is white. These samples establish alternating content, not its native-frame cadence.
defects.recommended_action: Inspect the complete S10/S11 boundary at native rate with audio to certify strobe and glitch execution.

overall.summary: Repair required. Fendi and the two-look structure remain legible, but product fidelity, outfit continuity and moving composites still fail. S12-WORDMARK-SCALE is RESOLVED in the supplied samples: lettering is no longer conspicuously oversized, although typography remains defective. S10 corridor visibility is repaired; cadence remains open. S07-CUT-TIMING is UNCERTAIN, not proven resolved: no sample covers its prior disputed boundary interval. The old centered-white S11 mark and navy shoulder blocking are removed, but their broader branding/construction defects persist in new forms.

answers.evidence: S01@00:01.750, S08@00:27.750 and S12@00:42.250 retain the anchor's cap, glasses, beard, facial proportions and recognizable performance manner.
answers.question: 1. Does Fendi remain recognizably the same real person throughout the performance shots?
answers.answer: Recognizably yes, with moderate-to-high confidence. Facial smoothing is apparent, but no clear identity replacement is established. Exact preservation of original face pixels and performance timing cannot be certified from this strip.

answers.evidence: S01@00:02.750 shows body-worn denim; S06@00:17.250 shows a cropped, open jacket; S08@00:24.750 introduces contrasting sleeves.
answers.question: 2. Is the YSL / Saint Laurent wardrobe actually and convincingly worn by Fendi?
answers.answer: On-body, yes; convincingly product-true, no. Clothing follows the performer, but the denim finish and incompatible hook constructions prevent the garments from reading as faithful designer-commercial representations.

answers.evidence: S06@00:21.250 versus S08@00:23.750 changes jacket length and sleeves; S09@00:29.750 introduces ribbed cuffs and a different fit.
answers.question: 3. Does the wardrobe remain stable during movement?
answers.answer: Not across the sequence. Major construction resets occur between performance assets, while lettering and silhouette edges vary within shots. Sub-frame fabric flicker remains unassessable at this sampling rate.

answers.evidence: S06@00:19.250 has irregular glyphs; S11@00:36.250 has stacked pseudo-text; S12@00:40.250 retains malformed lettering.
answers.question: 4. Where exactly does the wordmark/logo break (draft timecodes)?
answers.answer: Visible problem intervals: S06 16.250–21.250; S08 23.750–29.250; S09 29.750–31.250; S11 33.750–39.250; S12 39.750–42.750. These are sampled extents, not frame-exact onset or clearance times.

answers.evidence: S11@00:35.750 shows a compact multi-row mark; S12@00:40.250 and S12@00:41.250 show relatively small horizontal lettering.
answers.question: 5. Is any lettering visibly oversized or mis-scaled relative to the reference, particularly S11 and S12?
answers.answer: No conspicuous S12 oversizing remains; that specific prior defect is resolved in these samples. S11 is incorrectly stacked rather than oversized. Cross-shot mark scale still resets, and exact reference scaling requires native-resolution measurement.

answers.evidence: S01@00:02.750 adds a red tab; S06@00:18.250 exposes a shirt hem below a shortened jacket; S11@00:35.750 changes the tie to broad stripes.
answers.question: 6. Are there other garment defects not listed in the ShotSpecs QA?
answers.answer: Yes: unreferenced pocket-tab branding, inconsistent jeans wash, exaggerated shirt-cuff/hem exposure, and changing tie patterns. Full-outfit regeneration introduced additional continuity obligations without maintaining them.

answers.evidence: S02@00:04.750 enlarges soft seams and buttons; S04@00:12.750 shows smoothed facial detail; S11@00:34.750 has jagged extraction edges absent from the source contact sheet.
answers.question: 7. Does the native-resolution transformation/upscale visibly hurt quality relative to the source contact sheet?
answers.answer: Transformation artifacts visibly reduce realism. Attribution specifically to upscale or native-resolution processing is UNCERTAIN, low confidence: neither matched native source crops nor the full-resolution export is supplied.

answers.evidence: S03@00:11.750 retains knob-like hardware; S06@00:16.250 has a dark lower-right mass; S08@00:23.750 retains a flank fragment.
answers.question: 8. Does the environment composite convincingly eliminate the original closet?
answers.answer: No. The large door, shelving and hanging-clothes layout is replaced, but attached remnants survive. Exact identification of every fragment is uncertain; their incompatibility with the new room is clear.

answers.evidence: S08@00:24.250 has a rectangular forearm extension; S11@00:34.750 has stepped sleeve extrusions; S11@00:36.750 has a broad shoulder echo.
answers.question: 9. Do matte/composite boundaries remain believable during movement?
answers.answer: No. Moving boundaries alternate between soft halos and substantial retained patches. These artifacts make the performer appear extracted onto a sharp plate rather than photographed in the room.

answers.evidence: S02@00:04.250 is a soft torso crop; S07@00:22.250 presents cold wet city lights; S10@00:31.750 presents a reflective corridor.
answers.question: 10. Does B-roll feel intentional and compatible with the treatment?
answers.answer: Mostly in motif, not uniformly in execution. City and corridor inserts belong to the cold luxury world. The hardware insert fails its product-detail purpose; the diamond supplies the requested ice motif.

answers.evidence: S05@00:15.250 shows the diamond; S06@00:15.750 is white; S10@00:33.250 is white before performance resumes.
answers.question: 11. Do transitions work musically and visually?
answers.answer: The diamond-to-flash-to-hook progression is visually legible. Musical landing, strobe cadence and S11's glitch execution remain UNCERTAIN, low confidence without audio and native-rate boundary frames.

answers.evidence: S03@00:06.250, S08@00:23.750 and S11@00:33.750 visibly resume the performer after inserts.
answers.question: 12. Does the edit return correctly to synchronized performance after B-roll/FX?
answers.answer: It returns to performance in the intended slots. Correct synchronization is unverified, not failed by evidence. S09 additionally requires source-in-point verification.

answers.evidence: S04@00:12.750 confirms the punch-in; S09@00:29.750 confirms crossed arms; S10@00:31.750 confirms corridor content.
answers.question: 13. Does every shot substantially conform to its ShotSpec?
answers.answer: No. S01/03/04 fail garment/matte/mirror gates; S02 fails hardware truth; S05's motif conforms, beat timing unverified; S06/08/09/11/12 fail wardrobe/branding/compositing; S07's motif conforms; S10's corridor conforms, cadence unverified. Framing and crossed-arm intent generally survive.

answers.evidence: S01@00:01.750 establishes dark-room performance; S06@00:17.250 changes wardrobe and mirror world; S07@00:22.250 adds the night-city motif.
answers.question: 14. Does the complete sequence resemble the intended luxury fashion-commercial and high-energy rap treatment?
answers.answer: The treatment structure survives: performance, two looks, drop transformation and cold luxury inserts. Execution falls short of designer-commercial credibility because garment truth and integration fail. Musical energy cannot be fully judged from silent samples.

answers.evidence: S03@00:06.750 retains the source-like arm-up delivery; S08@00:24.250 exposes extraction artifacts; S11@00:36.250 displays fabricated branding.
answers.question: 15. Does this look like a REAL Fendi music video enhanced by AVT, or AI content built around Fendi's song?
answers.answer: It remains recognizably Fendi's performance, not a demonstrated synthetic replacement. However, the current finish reads as AI-styled compositing around that performance rather than convincing enhancement: unstable products and visible extraction repeatedly become the subject.

answers.evidence: S06@00:21.250 precedes S07@00:21.750; neither samples 21.514–21.681. S04@00:14.750 still contains incoming diamond content under the outgoing label.
answers.question: Re-review audit: are the previous cut-label timing defects resolved?
answers.answer: S07-CUT-TIMING is UNCERTAIN, low confidence, because its disputed interval is unsampled. SEQ-CUT-BOUNDARY-OFFSET remains present as a smaller label/ownership discrepancy; the old approximately 0.041-second magnitude is not verified.

escalate_to_fendi: No treatment change is needed for the objective repairs. After garment and matte correction, request Fendi's full-motion authenticity approval: S08@00:24.250 and S11@00:36.250 currently let extraction and fabricated branding compete with his performance.

Do not approve musical timing from this strip. Review the audible native-frame export, especially the drop, S10/S11 transition and final hard out; supplied samples S06@00:15.750 and S10@00:33.250 only establish white FX states.
